title: Love is stronger
hook: the Christian hope is that love is stronger than death

segments.voice: Yesterday, the groaning Spirit: groanings which cannot be uttered. Your line was the spirit prays. Was there a moment you let one long breath out be enough? Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

A gravestone with two names carved on it. One has both dates filled in. The other has the first date, and a blank space after the dash, waiting. Somebody chose that stone. They stood in an office and decided their name would go next to the person they loved, even though they're still alive. It's a strange, stubborn thing to do. It says: death has taken one of us, and it still hasn't separated us. Whether that can be true is an old question. The Bible has a few lines that answer it. Today: love is stronger.

Start with a love song. In the Song of Songs, near the end, the beloved says, in the King James words: "Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death." Strong as death. Not stronger. As strong. That alone is daring. Death is hard to argue with, and here a love poem calls it an even match. Then: "Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it." Now go back to the chapter we read yesterday, Romans 8. Later in the same chapter as the groaning Spirit, Paul makes a list of everything that could possibly cut people off from God's love, and he puts death first: "For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord." Neither death. That's where the Christian hope steps past the love song, from as strong to stronger. And the reason Christians give is Easter: the belief that Jesus died and rose, so that death didn't have the last say over love. Paul elsewhere taunts death with a question: "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?" Churches describe what that hope means for those who have died in different ways, and much of it they leave with God. But the hope itself is plain in these lines. Love doesn't make death painless. The stone still has a name on it. The hope is that death doesn't get to separate what love has joined to God.

Here's the practice: love someone today. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind someone you love who is still here. Then, if there is one, someone you love who has died. Hold them both for a moment, side by side, like two names on one stone. If you pray, you can thank God for each of them by name. Then come back to the one still here. Choose one act of love for them today: a call, a meal, a word you've been meaning to say. Something that won't wait for a better time. The bell holds the time.
Love is stronger. The Song of Songs says love is strong as death. Paul says not even death can separate us from the love of God. That is the Christian hope.
Your line: love is stronger. Today, do the one act of love you chose, before the day gets away from you. Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Christians read Romans 8:38–39 and 1 Corinthians 15 at funerals and on Easter, and the Song of Songs' line about love and death is sometimes read at weddings; some churches also remember the dead by name in their prayers.

original.note: Hebrew: love, in the line love is strong as death, Song of Songs 8:6.

trapdoor: what you thought: love makes losing someone hurt less.
what it means: the Christian hope is that nothing, not even death, can separate people from the love of God.
what a scholar hears: the love song says strong as death, an even match. Romans 8 and Easter carry the hope one step further, to stronger.

notes: Hebrew אַהֲבָה; the original-game note says it is the last word of the 8:6 phrase ('azzah khammavet ahavah'). Confirm.
The index title 'love is stronger' goes beyond Song 8:6 ('strong as death'); the script says so plainly and grounds 'stronger' in Romans 8:38–39 and the resurrection.

'Churches describe what that hope means for the people we've lost in different ways' covers differing teaching on the dead (resurrection, intermediate state, prayers for the dead). Keeper may want to be more specific.
